overallAssessment.verdict: The Snowdonia data file (data/regions/snowdonia.ts) and editorial markdown (content/regions/snowdonia.md) together represent an exceptionally strong content foundation — the most comprehensive region coverage in the codebase. The markdown in particular is high quality, accurate and editorially distinctive. Three material blockers prevent advancement to published: (1) the hero image snowdonia-hero.jpg was added in a commit titled 'add image generation skill and download region/activity images' (Feb 2026) with no source URL in the image registry — origin and licence are unknown, and the commit message cannot rule out AI generation; (2) all pricing in topExperiences is sourced from 'Perplexity research' per the ts file header, violating the no-AI-content policy; (3) the UNESCO heritage entry in snowdonia.ts is vague ('UNESCO-related slate landscapes') and does not correctly name the designation — the markdown correctly names it 'Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales, inscribed 2021'. Beyond these blockers the content contains several facts needing human verification (dark sky reserve count, visitor numbers, Aber Falls parking fee) and a small set of content gaps between the ts and md files.
overallAssessment.structuralQuality: VERY HIGH — snowdonia.ts covers hero prose, 10 keyFacts, 10 bestFor activities, 4-season guide, 10 insiderTips, 12 topExperiences, 10 FAQs, 6 hiddenGems, 6 localEatsAndDrinks, and full SEO meta. snowdonia.md adds a further 6 sections not represented in the ts structure (mountain ranges, dark skies, slate country, Welsh language primer, 'what it's NOT good for', weather reality, getting here).
overallAssessment.factualConfidence: MEDIUM-HIGH — core geography, park establishment date, peak height, UNESCO inscription, Dark Sky Reserve status, and Welsh language character are well-established. Pricing, visitor figures, dark sky reserve count, and Aber Falls parking fee need live verification.

area_823sqmiles.claim: 823 sq miles (2,131 km²), Wales' largest national park
area_823sqmiles.verdict: VERIFIED — Eryri National Park Authority confirms the park area as 2,132 km² (823 sq miles). It is Wales' largest national park.

highestPeak_1085m.claim: Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) at 1,085m (3,560ft) — highest in England & Wales
highestPeak_1085m.verdict: VERIFIED — Yr Wyddfa is 1,085m (3,560ft), the highest peak in both Wales and England. Established by Ordnance Survey.

established_1951.claim: Established 1951, third UK national park after Peak District and Lake District
established_1951.verdict: VERIFIED — Snowdonia was designated in 1951 as the third national park in the UK. Peak District (1951, first), Lake District (1951, second), Snowdonia (1951, third) — all three were designated in the same year but the Peak District was the first to be formally confirmed.
established_1951.note: The 'third' ordering is widely cited and correct.

peaks_15over3000ft.verdict: VERIFIED — There are exactly 15 Welsh peaks over 3,000ft (914m). The Welsh 3000s challenge links all 15 in a single push (~30 miles, ~13,000ft ascent). The Eryri NPA and all major mountaineering sources confirm this figure.

lakes_100plus.claim: 100+ natural lakes including Llyn Llydaw, Glaslyn, and Bala (largest in Wales)
lakes_100plus.verdict: APPROXIMATELY CORRECT — Eryri contains well over 100 natural lakes. Llyn Tegid (Bala Lake) is correctly cited as the largest natural lake in Wales. Llyn Llydaw and Glaslyn are correctly within the Snowdon massif. Note: Llyn Tegid is at the very south-eastern edge of the park; some sources place it as adjacent rather than central.

population_26000.claim: ~26,000, main hubs Llanberis (~2,000) and Blaenau Ffestiniog (~6,000)
population_26000.verdict: APPROXIMATELY CORRECT — 2021 census data gives Eryri (Snowdonia National Park) a resident population of approximately 26,000. Llanberis and Blaenau Ffestiniog are the principal settlements. The sub-figures (~2,000 and ~6,000) are plausible but settlement census data varies by enumeration boundary.
population_26000.confidence: MEDIUM — overall figure correct, sub-figures directionally right

annualVisitors_6million.claim: 6+ million, Snowdon summit sees 600,000+ hikers annually
annualVisitors_6million.verdict: NEEDS_VERIFICATION — The 600,000+ figure for Snowdon summit is widely cited by Eryri NPA and Visit Wales. The 6+ million park-wide visitor count is at the high end of typical estimates. Eryri NPA and NPAP figures have historically quoted 3-4 million annual visits to the national park, though day-tripper counting methodologies vary.
annualVisitors_6million.action: HUMAN REVIEW — verify current Eryri NPA visitor count figures against their latest annual/economic impact report. If the 6 million figure cannot be sourced, rephrase to 'millions of visitors each year' or cite the confirmed 600,000 Snowdon figure as the verifiable headline.
annualVisitors_6million.confidence: MEDIUM-LOW — Snowdon 600k is widely verified; park total of 6m+ needs source

darkSkyReserve.claim: International Dark Sky Reserve, one of only 18 worldwide
darkSkyReserve.verdict: PARTIALLY OUTDATED — Eryri became an International Dark Sky Reserve (IDSR) in 2015, confirmed by the International Dark-Sky Association. However, '18 worldwide' was accurate around 2015–2016 at time of designation; as of 2024 there are approximately 22–23 IDSRs globally. The reserve status itself is correct; the count of '18' is outdated.
darkSkyReserve.action: Update '18 worldwide' to the current IDA count or rephrase to 'one of a small number of International Dark Sky Reserves worldwide'. The reserve designation itself is not in doubt.
darkSkyReserve.confidence: HIGH for status; LOW for count figure

welshNameEryri.verdict: CORRECT — Both translations are linguistically defended. 'Land of eagles' (*eryr* = eagle) is the popular etymology. 'Highlands' is the modern scholarly preference given the absence of eagles in historical recorded memory. The Eryri NPA itself uses both explanations without definitively settling the debate.

unescoSlate.claim: snowdonia.ts: 'UNESCO-related slate landscapes, Gwynedd slate sites recognized for industrial heritage'
unescoSlate.verdict: INCOMPLETE — the ts data file understates this. The correct designation is 'Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales' (Welsh: Tirwedd Llechi Cymru), a serial UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in July 2021 (WHC reference 1654). This is the full, proper name. The markdown (content/regions/snowdonia.md) correctly states the inscription year (2021) and the full name. The ts data field should be updated to match.
unescoSlate.action: Update data/regions/snowdonia.ts keyFacts[Heritage] label to: 'Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales — UNESCO WHS (inscribed 2021)'. This is verifiable and significant — it should be stated precisely.

heroContent.verdict: EXCELLENT — the ts heroContent is vivid, specific, and accurately characterises Snowdonia. References to Crib Goch, zip wires at 100mph, underground trampolines, the Afon Conwy/Glaslyn/Llugwy, and the Welsh name 'Eryri' are all factually grounded. The snowdonia.md takes this further with granular mountain range breakdowns (Glyderau, Carneddau, Rhinogs, Cadair Idris, Moel Siabod) that are accurate and editorially distinctive.

tsVsMdAudit.verdict: The ts data file and md editorial content are broadly consistent and complementary. The md is significantly richer in mountain-range detail, cultural framing (Welsh language, slate heritage), and honest gap-flagging ('What It's NOT Good For'). No material factual conflicts identified between the two files. The md in several areas is more current and precise (UNESCO inscription year, dark sky year, 'noticeably less busy' instead of '40% less busy').
discrepancies: ts: UNESCO 'UNESCO-related slate landscapes' vs md: 'Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales — UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 2021)'. The md is correct and more precise.
ts insiderTips: 'Tuesday-Thursday slots are 40% less busy than weekends' vs md: 'Tuesday–Thursday slots are noticeably less busy'. The md is more appropriately hedged.
ts localEatsAndDrinks: 6 venues, no Pen-y-Gwryd Hotel. md: includes Pen-y-Gwryd. Recommend adding to ts.
ts topExperiences: 12 experiences; md Smart Play mentions Go Below (Cwmorthin) and Antur Stiniog, neither of which appear in the ts list.
mdStrengths: Mountain range breakdowns (Glyderau, Carneddau, Rhinogs, Cadair Idris, Moel Siabod) with accurate scramble grade notes — absent from ts
Dedicated dark skies section with four specific stargazing spots (Llyn Geirionydd, Llynnau Cregennen, Crimea Pass, Llyn y Dywarchen)
Slate country section with Dinorwig, Llechwedd, Penrhyn, Cwmorthin/Croesor, and Ffestiniog Railway detailed
Welsh language primer (cwm, llyn, bwlch, afon, moel, carnedd, coed) — distinctive and accurate
'What It's NOT Good For' — editorial honesty about coasteering, sandy beaches, and car-dependency is rare and strong
Aberglaslyn Pass as hidden gem — not in ts hiddenGems array
Pen-y-Gwryd Hotel — historically significant, correctly described as 1953 Everest training base

topBlockers.blocker: UNESCO heritage field in snowdonia.ts is vague and incorrect — does not name the actual World Heritage designation
topBlockers.detail: data/regions/snowdonia.ts keyFacts entry reads: { label: 'Heritage', value: 'UNESCO-related slate landscapes', detail: 'Gwynedd slate sites recognized for industrial heritage' }. This is both vague and technically inaccurate — 'UNESCO-related' implies association rather than full inscription. The correct designation is 'Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales' (Welsh: Tirwedd Llechi Cymru), a serial UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in July 2021 (WHC reference 1654). The content/regions/snowdonia.md correctly states 'Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales — UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 2021)'. Publishing the vague ts version when the correct official name is freely available from UNESCO would be a factual embarrassment, particularly given that this is one of Wales' most significant recent heritage designations.
topBlockers.resolution: Update data/regions/snowdonia.ts keyFacts[Heritage] to: { label: 'Heritage', value: 'Slate Landscape of Northwest Wales', detail: 'UNESCO World Heritage Site, inscribed July 2021 (WHC 1654)' }. Source: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1654. This is a one-line change with a verified source that can be made immediately.
